episodes.199254: A shortwave trough moved through Arkansas early on March 13, with convection eventually refiring in parts of Central Alabama along a boundary that had moved east from the Mississippi Valley. A storm just after 8 AM produced up to nickel-size hail in the Winfield and Ethridge areas. More activity formed in the late evening across northwest Alabama, with a cell moving southeastward into Winston County and dropping nickel-size hail near Double Springs.
episodes.199277: A narrow convective boundary marking the nocturnal Cuba landbreeze boundary moved northward, passing through the Lower Florida Keys with scattered convective rain showers.  A few waterspouts were observed near the Lower Florida Keys as the convective boundary moved northward from the Straits of Florida into the Gulf waters north of Key West.
episodes.199875: An isolated afternoon thunderstorm was able to tap into modest instability to become strong and eventually generate severe hail. The storm originated in the south Columbus area before dropping 1��� hail in south Marion County.
episodes.200049: From March 11th through 13th a winter storm brought heavy mountain snow, strong southerly winds and moderate to heavy rain to interior northern California. Snow amounts of 1 to over 3 feet were observed in the mountains. Roadway flooding was observed in the Valley and foothills, with downed trees and powerlines from strong southerly winds. On March 12th a line of non-severe storms moved through portions of the Sacramento Valley producing wind gusts over 50 mph. This resulted in a large oak tree to fall and damage an apartment building in Sacramento County. As the line of storms moved through the foothills, numerous trees and powerlines came down leading to power outages in the area. Traffic was being turned on Interstate 80 at Alta for a period due to spinouts and heavy snow.
episodes.200171: A moist and unstable airmass with steep mid-level lapse rates ahead of a cold front resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms.  Large hail occurred across southeast Alabama, and sporadic wind damage occurred across the Florida panhandle. One tornado occurred in southwest Georgia.
episodes.200173: A moist and unstable airmass with steep mid-level lapse rates ahead of a cold front resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms.  Large hail occurred across southeast Alabama, and sporadic wind damage occurred across the Florida panhandle. One tornado occurred in southwest Georgia.
episodes.200419: On the morning of March 13th, a west to east oriented cold front was pushing south near the Ohio River, but it stalled before pushing back north. This left central Kentucky in the warm sector with warm moist air moving in from the south. As the system's north to south oriented cold front moved east through the Lower Ohio Valley on the 15th, several storms produced widespread hail across north central Kentucky. Some of these storms also produced localized damaging winds and flooding by the 16th as the system's second reinforcing cold front pushed east through the area.
episodes.200620: A pair of strong shortwave troughs moved from the Desert Southwest into the Plains Wednesday through Friday (March 12-14), generating isolated severe thunderstorms, strong non-thunderstorm winds and critical fire weather conditions across the region. A High Wind Warning was issued on March 14th for the northeastern half of the region.
episodes.201177: A strong Pacific storm system brought locally heavy snow, isolated high winds, and isolated minor flooding to southeast California.
episodes.201294: A strong area of low pressure transitioned over the region and brought heavy rain, mountain snow, and some strong and gusty winds for the higher elevations and deserts.
episodes.203682: A late-season winter storm brought numerous weather hazards to Southwestern California. Rainfall totals generally ranged between 0.50 and 1.50 inches across coastal areas up to 4 inches in the mountains. Winter storm conditions developed in the mountains with snowfall totals up to 18 inches and southerly wind gusts up to 77 MPH.  Thunderstorms, associated with this system, brought some reports of flooding as well as a weak tornado.

events.narrative: A roof was blown off a house and trees were damaged near Slocum.
Strong winds brought down a tree that was blocking Old Foresthill Road and State Route 49.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding bringing traffic to a standstill at Interstate 80 West and Northgate Boulevard due to heavy rain.
A thunderstorm wind gust, estimated to be 60 MPH, impacted the USFS Fire Station on Figueroa Road. The thunderstorm gust knocked out a window in the engine bay.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 65 MPH was reported at Saddle Peak in the Santa Monica Mountains.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 58 MPH was reported in Redondo Beach, along the coast of Los Angeles county.
A brief, weak tornado developed in the community of Pico Rivera in Los Angeles county. The short-lived tornado uprooted several trees, knocked down numerous branches and caused some roof damage.
Strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flash flooding in the city of Los Angeles. At the intersection of Highway 101 and Campo de Cahuenga, significant road flooding was reported.
Public source reported 1.81 inch of rain, 0.5 inch snow.

Delayed report. Swift water rescues. Vehicles in mud, debris and water. 6 persons  affected. Mud was half way up the side of one vehicle and drivers were trapped. 3  automated weather stations recorded 0.5 inches in 1 hour. Several mud slides reported.
Penny to nickel-size hail fell in Winfield, with hail covering the ground.
Nickel-size hail fell in the Eldridge area.
There was minor flooding and mud on the Goffs Rd offramp from I-40.
